approach: Check whether zero net force truly rules out every other motion for a rigid body, then check the reason's kinematic claim on its own.

steps.text: Zero net force fixes only the motion of the center of mass: it must move at constant velocity, which may or may not be zero.

A rigid body can still rotate about its center of mass while the net force stays zero, if a net torque acts on it. Rotation is something else that can happen, so the assertion's claim that nothing else can happen is false.
Check the reason on its own: constant velocity means the velocity does not change with time, so its time derivative, the acceleration, is zero.
The reason is a correct kinematic statement by itself, but the assertion is false, so the reason cannot be its explanation. This matches: Assertion false, Reason true.

final_answer.value: (d) The Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming zero net force fully determines a rigid body's motion, missing that it can still rotate, leads to marking the Assertion true and picking option (a).
